Practical.title: SQL — Practical
Practical.body:
Q: What is a Thread in Java?
Ans
• A thread is a lightweight subprocess, the smallest unit of processing. Multithreading allows concurrent execution of two or more parts of a program.

Q: What is the role of the JVM?
Ans
• JVM acts as a run-time engine to run Java applications. It loads, verifies, and executes code while providing a runtime environment.

Q: What are the four pillars of OOPs?
Ans
• The four pillars are Inheritance, Polymorphism, Encapsulation, and Abstraction.

Q: Difference between String and StringBuilder?
Ans
• String is immutable (cannot be changed), whereas StringBuilder is mutable and more efficient for frequent modifications.

Q: Interface vs Abstract Class?
Ans
• Interfaces support multiple inheritance and have only abstract methods (pre-Java 8), while abstract classes can have constructors and concrete methods.

Q: What is Exception Handling?
Ans
• It is a mechanism to handle runtime errors using try, catch, finally, throw, and throws keywords to maintain normal application flow.
